scope: R1 development fixture packaging only; no W20/A15/final release/LIVE acceptance

findings.title: Stop can terminate a different fixture sharing the same release executable
findings.trigger: Two independent fresh data directories A and B launch the same release bin/control.exe. A stale or incorrect PID record in A names the B process.
findings.actual: stop.ps1 -DataDir A succeeds, kills B and leaves A healthy; only the shared executable path is checked.
findings.impact: A stale/reused PID record can terminate another running fixture or instance from the same release directory. Data directory selection is not bound to the process being stopped.
findings.required_fix: Record and verify process creation identity plus a launch-instance/data-directory binding before destructive stop. Reject mismatches without stopping either process, preserve data, and retain an explicit recoverable stale-record path.

findings.title: A package labelled with a frozen Git commit includes dirty and untracked inputs
findings.trigger: Detached HEAD remains 14bf6d6 while a tracked installation README contains an uncommitted synthetic marker and release/independent-untracked.json is untracked.
findings.actual: The actual offline build exits zero and packages both markers; manifest.source_commit still names the clean frozen revision. source_tree_sha256 describes the selected bytes but is never bound to that Git tree.
findings.impact: The release artifact cannot be reproduced from its declared source_commit alone. Changes during dependency/build steps can also mix packaged source with compiled input because no stable source snapshot or pre/post check exists.
findings.required_fix: Build from the exact pinned Git tree or reject changed/untracked build inputs and verify source bytes before and after the build. Ensure the source manifest and binaries originate from that same immutable input.

limits: Original author two-build equality, wrong-tool rejection and 18-case output are hash-verified source evidence. The full 18-case harness is not redundantly rerun; independent actual ZIP/Git comparison, start/stop and dirty-build negatives target the unresolved boundaries.

Only reviewer-owned fresh credential-free fixture processes, data directories, an isolated sparse Git checkout, and owned output ZIPs were used. No existing product/protected service, production database, holdout payload or provider was accessed.

The builder uses pinned Go/Node/npm, offline dependency resolution, trimpath binaries, sorted ZIP entries and fixed ZIP timestamps. The independent negative harness also invoked the hash-pinned Python interpreter.
The manifest honestly reports 27 license-text gaps, release.reproduce UNBOUND, unqualified runtime/provider identity, final upgrade not implemented, A15 clean Windows not run and W20 not accepted.

Bundled construction source is not a standalone full execution environment: tool locks are external and the project-cycle fixture contract is absent. Existing source_checkout_required restrictions remain; this is not a complete final source/rebuild distribution claim.
Existing policy-denied temporary cleanup paths were untouched. All observed stop actions concerned only the two newly launched known fixture PIDs.
